prompt:
Design a desktop website landing screen, 16:9 landscape (1920x1080), rendered as the web page itself edge to edge (no browser window, no device frame, no mockup).

Brand: ROOMi (ROOMiVERSE), a DJ lifestyle brand: "turn any ordinary room into your own party". Use the attached image as the logo: a hand-drawn marker graffiti wordmark "ROOMi".

The site is art-directed as a 1980s Madrid underground scene magazine cover: printed cheaply on white paper in fluorescent hot pink #F71D64, violet #C14ED4 and black #111111, inks slightly misregistered at every edge.

Regions, in order:
1. Masthead: the ROOMi graffiti logo huge across the top center as if hand-inked that afternoon, with "ROOMiVERSE" small beside it. This doubles as the site header.
2. A flash-lit photograph cropped hard and bleeding off the frame: a stack of shipping containers at a port at night, hit by direct camera flash, harsh shadow, one container door open.
3. Navigation as cover lines scattered across the cover at four different angles, no shared baseline, each one a clickable menu item in bold condensed sans: "MEET ROOMi", "WHAT'S GOING ON: 6 PARTIES", "LET'S PARTY", "SHOP", plus small "CART (0)" and "MY" at the top right corner, set straight.
4. One cover line larger than the rest, in a pink block: "ENTER THE CONTAINER →" as the main action.
5. Bottom strip like a magazine issue line: "ISSUE 001 · 내 방안의 나만의 우주".

One dominant move: the flash photo under the hand-inked masthead. Readable, not chaotic noise. No fake prices, no extra UI cards.
